Abeloth research extraction (Wookieepedia / Star Wars Legends)

Source checked: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Abeloth
Final URL: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Abeloth (no redirect)
Legends subpage check: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Abeloth/Legends does not exist; the main page is categorized/tagged as a Legends article. Extraction is from the main page.
The page's Notes and references section was scrolled/read. Bracketed numbers below are the article's footnote numbers, not independently verified claims.

ARTICLE SECTIONS AND LORE

[Once upon a time -> Older but just never wiser; Marooned]
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)
- The article says Abeloth began as a mortal Servant to the Ones (Father, Son, Daughter), later becoming their Mother/peacekeeper. She drank from the Font of Power and bathed in the Pool of Knowledge; the article attributes her immortality and dark-side power to that corruption [1][2].
- The article says the corrupted Mother subdued the Son and Daughter, while the Father protected them and left Abeloth stranded. Her anger corrupted her planet; she could control its vegetation, including making overgrown plants prey on animals unless she wanted otherwise [1][7].
- The article says the Son and Daughter repeatedly defeated/contained Abeloth over thousands of years, using Killik-built wonders including Centerpoint and Sinkhole Station to imprison her in the Maw [1][6].

[All alone?]
- The article states that the Father, Son, and Daughter were the Ones of Mortis. During Anakin Skywalker's Mortis encounter, all three Ones were slain with the Dagger of Mortis, described as the only weapon against their immortality—and Abeloth's [1][18][21]. The Dagger and Mortis then vanished [21]. This is the article's direct immortality scaling; it does not say Abeloth was equal to each One in every ability.
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)

[Incipient tendrils; Emerging enigma; A stare directly at the Maw…]
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)
- Abeloth absorbed Callista Ming and could use both of Ming's bodies/forms [4][11]. As a child, Ben Skywalker sensed Abeloth's dark “tentacle of need” at Shelter; other vulnerable Jedi children were also contacted [3][7].
- Abeloth's psychosis made affected Jedi think others were impostors and gave them esoteric Force abilities far beyond their normal skillsets [7][11]. One affected Jedi disarmed multiple soldiers, paralyzed them, and ran at great speed with abilities associated with Darth Caedus [26].
- Abeloth reached into Allana Solo's mind from Kessel's garrison moon and frightened her [4][23][28].
  Source: Fate of the Jedi: Outcast ; Fate of the Jedi: Allies [per Wookieepedia "Abeloth" rev 15688755, ref 28,4; approximate match 0.69, verify; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]

CONCRETE FEATS AND BATTLES

[Monster on a hill; Foe on the beach; Addicted to betrayal]
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)
- A Sith apprentice struck Abeloth with a lightsaber and was immediately incapacitated and thrown into a cavern wall. Abeloth suspended Vestara Khai in the air and later controlled/commanded the Sith Meditation Sphere Ship [7].
- Abeloth controlled the carnivorous plant life on her world; none of the plants attacked while she was nearby [7]. Vestara alone saw her true form among the Sith and recognized the betrayal [7].

[Bad omen; Terrified to look down]
- At the Font of Power, Luke Skywalker approached Abeloth's manifested true form beyond shadows. The article says a tentacle entered and moved up inside Luke's leg; Abeloth tried to lure him by using a familiar, dream-lover-like voice, but he withdrew [7].
- Beyond shadows, the dead Mara Jade warned Luke that Abeloth was “one of the old ones” and told him to leave her alone; this is a character statement/warning, not a measured feat [7].

[Dance with the devil]
- Abeloth used the Force to seize Vestara Khai and strike her with lightning; Khai deflected it back. Abeloth fought Luke Skywalker, High Lord Sarasu Taalon, Gavar Khai, and other Sith, disappeared/reappeared during the fight, and was constrained enough by the Sith control web that the web stifled her powers and frightened her [4].
- Abeloth then released a massive Force wave that repulsed all her attackers and fled. She killed the Sith left guarding Dyon Stadd. Luke cut through Stadd's body, revealing that Abeloth had switched bodies; the apparent Abeloth body had died, while Abeloth survived in Stadd's form [4][11].

[Playing with fire; Desperate prayers]
- On Pydyr, Abeloth used illusions and fear against the Sith and Fallanassi. When Luke fought the Akanah avatar, he flung Taalon away, kicked Abeloth without effect, severed her arm with his lightsaber, cut her leg, and pushed her into a pit [11].
- Abeloth survived the fall, came onto Luke, held him down, drove her severed arm into his throat, pressed against his larynx, and bent his knee with her strength. Luke snapped three of her ribs and activated his lightsaber through her stomach “to no avail.” He splashed lava onto her back; she wailed and had to sustain her body through the Force [11].
- Luke lifted a ceiling beam that crushed Abeloth against him. Akanah resisted possession, and Luke's lightsaber then cut through Abeloth's flank and killed that manifestation [11]. This is a concrete kill of a manifestation, not proof of permanent death.

[Lit from within; Take the battle overground]
- Luke used a dark-side variant of mnemotherapy to tear Callista Ming's spirit/consciousness out of Abeloth. The article says the act severely weakened Abeloth; Ming glowed and became one with the Force [32].
- On Nam Chorios, Abeloth's possessed Nenn killed himself, weakening her. Abeloth escaped in Ship; Vestara's killing of a tsil caused a death convulsion that debilitated Abeloth. A Jedi shadow bomb also caused pain through the Force, and Luke's attack damaged Ship, but Abeloth escaped. The article says she was left weaker than ever [32].

[All she did was smile; At the same time]
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)
- In the final battle beyond shadows, Luke fought Abeloth while both used their Force essences. Luke's Force blast made her sag by the Lake of Apparitions; he struck her legs, throat, and head, constricted her larynx, and lost a knee of her form. Abeloth struck Luke's right eye [1].
- Darth Krayt drove his fingers into Abeloth's stomach and drained her power. Krayt, Luke, and Abeloth became entangled in a Force-energy struggle; the article says Abeloth was weakened faster than Luke while Krayt drained her, but the drain also harmed Krayt and Luke [1].
- Abeloth tore away her energy bond with Luke and tried to bite them. Luke merged his form with hers again and urged Krayt to pull harder. Krayt recalled a severed hand lodged in Abeloth; Abeloth then tore at both men and left each with a fist-sized hole in the chest while she escaped with some of their Force essence [1].
- At the Font, Ben Skywalker used a Force blast that the article describes as strong enough to knock a frigate out of a planet's orbit; Abeloth resisted it, shifting only a couple of centimeters. A pillar then bypassed her Force barrier, damaging her eye, skull, brain, and drawing blood [1][11].

[Sets the scene; Pierced through the heart]
- In the astral realm, Abeloth's Force lightning passed through Darth Krayt and hit Luke before Krayt could attack; it blasted Krayt backward [1].
- At the Font, Abeloth wrestled Vestara Khai. Ben drove a shikkar through Abeloth's back, spinal cord, and heart; Khai hit her with lightning, and Ben dragged her into sunlight and crushed her chest with a pillar fragment. The article records this as the final physical assault, but Ship says Abeloth was dead “as much as that is possible” [1].
- The article says Krayt left Luke after stating that Sith dominance had only been delayed by Caedus and Abeloth. This is Krayt's statement about the future, not a feat [1].

[Checkmate; Clarity in death?; The wound that would not close]
  Source: UNRESOLVED (sentence not found in current Wookieepedia article revision; primary source not identified)
- Saba Sebatyne fought an Abeloth manifestation at the Jedi Temple computer core. Abeloth tried to pump dark Force essence into Saba as a replacement avatar; Saba cut off the tendrils, smashed a hole through Abeloth's fangs, tore her throat, bit through skin, cartilage, muscle, bone, and spinal cord, and removed her head. Saba and Tahiri each reported killing an Abeloth [1].
- Abeloth's Coruscant assault left hundreds of kilometers dark, caused ruins/fires and volcanic ash, and the article attributes billions of casualties to the resulting volcanic devastation [1]. The Jedi Council believed she would recover and return, though not in their lifetimes [1].
- Luke retained a severe chest wound from Abeloth that cost him a rib and part of a lung [1][41]. The Jedi sought the Dagger of Mortis to make her permanent death possible [1].

POWERS, FEATS, AND ARTICLE-STATED SCALING

[Powers and abilities -> Unlimited power]
- Concrete abilities listed by the article: command of native flora; long-range mind influence/psychosis; possession and body-switching; shapeshifting; teleportation over short distances; Force lightning; Tutaminis; exceptional telekinesis; Force healing; Force flight; pyrokinesis/cryokinesis; remote lightsaber deactivation; Flow Walking; Technometry; Force barriers; Force scream; and feeding on fear, anguish, and death [1][4][5][7][11][32].
- Abeloth could call/command Ship across the galaxy. Ship was programmed to obey the strongest will, and the article says Abeloth's will overrode the efforts of both Sith and Jedi to control it [4].
- Avatar dependency is a stated weakness: killing avatar bodies weakened her rapidly; destroying all could result in “death.” Non-Force-sensitive hosts deteriorated more quickly. The article says Luke used this weakness to deliver the finishing blow [1].
- The article says Abeloth could have three manifestations at once after feeding on Coruscant's suffering; it says she could make monsters from dead bodies and inhabit a computer [1].
- The article says Abeloth was not invincible: manifestations could be annihilated by a thermal detonator, and blades, lightsabers, blasters, or Force-thrown objects could wound her if they bypassed her guard [1][4][11]. Krayt's life-force drain harmed her and also harmed him and Luke [1].

ARTICLE'S EXPLICIT SCALING / HYPE (MARKED AS STATEMENTS, NOT FEATS)

- The article states Abeloth's physical strength augmentation was “a dozen times” Luke Skywalker's, while also stating Luke defeated her in a duel by raining debris on her [11]. This is the page's explicit Luke comparison; it is a cited statement, not an independently measured feat.
- The article calls her “an astonishingly powerful Force user” and says mortals could not understand her dark power [7]. Ship says Abeloth is older and more powerful than Jaina Solo can imagine [4]; Tahiri calls her a “living Force volcano,” and Jaina compares her to a nova [11][1]. These are character descriptions/hype, not feats.
- The article says Luke had encountered no more powerful use of Force Healing [32]. This is Luke's comparative assessment, not a quantified feat.
- The article says it was presumed Abeloth would become effectively all-powerful if allowed to feed on Coruscant's suffering for long enough [1]. “Presumed” marks this as an in-universe/authorial statement, not an achieved feat.
- The article says the Ones' Dagger of Mortis was the only weapon against their immortality and Abeloth's [1][21]. It separately says Abeloth could not be truly slain except by the Mortis Dagger, despite repeated avatar deaths [1][11].
  Source: Star Wars: The Clone Wars — "Ghosts of Mortis" ; Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse ; Fate of the Jedi: Vortex [per Wookieepedia "Abeloth" rev 15688755, ref 21,1,11; per-sentence approximate match (2/2 sentences matched, min 0.60), verify; agrees with the entry's own ref marker]
- The article says Troy Denning personally considered Abeloth gone for “a couple of dozen millennia” after Apocalypse [57]. This is an author's later opinion/statement, not an on-page feat or guaranteed future.
